items.visual_pattern: older leaves yellow first, general chlorosis progressing upward
items.common_confusion: magnesium deficiency or natural late flower fade
items.recommended_game_diagnostic_hint: Older leaves fade first; check feed strength and stage before diagnosing.

items.affected_leaf_age: older leaves and whole plant vigor
items.visual_pattern: darker dull foliage, slow growth, possible purple tones
items.common_confusion: cold stress or genetics-related purple coloration
items.recommended_game_diagnostic_hint: Dark slow plant with cool conditions may mimic phosphorus issues.

items.visual_pattern: marginal burn and edge necrosis, weak leaf edges
items.recommended_game_diagnostic_hint: Edge burn with weaker older leaves can point to potassium shortage.

items.affected_leaf_age: newer growth and actively transpiring leaves
items.visual_pattern: irregular rusty spots, small necrotic lesions, possible deformation
items.recommended_game_diagnostic_hint: Rusty spots on new growth suggest calcium availability problems.

items.visual_pattern: interveinal chlorosis with green veins remaining
items.recommended_game_diagnostic_hint: Green veins with yellowing between them on older leaves is a strong magnesium clue.

items.visual_pattern: even pale yellowing on young growth
items.recommended_game_diagnostic_hint: Younger leaves paling evenly suggests sulfur, but verify pH and feed history.

items.visual_pattern: young leaves yellow with greener veins early
items.recommended_game_diagnostic_hint: If new growth yellows first while older leaves stay greener, consider iron/pH lockout.
Speckled chlorosis can indicate manganese availability issues.

items.visual_pattern: small distorted new leaves, shortened internodes, chlorosis
items.recommended_game_diagnostic_hint: Distorted compact new growth plus chlorosis can suggest zinc issues.
